title: Breaking down barriers! OpenAI offers another 50,000 free Plus spots to researchers worldwide
excerpt: OpenAI recently announced the official expansion of its free ChatGPT access program for academic researchers, aiming to provide free access to frontier AI model
content_html:
OpenAI recently announced the official expansion of its free ChatGPT access program for academic researchers, aiming to provide free access to frontier AI models to up to 200,000 researchers worldwide. A new round of applications will officially open on November 23 local time, with 50,000 new free slots planned.

In terms of operating mechanism, this expansion adjusts the allocation rules and service tiers. The new slots will completely move away from the lottery mechanism used in the previous pilot phase and switch to a "first-come, first-served" allocation method. Regarding service tiers, based on analysis of actual usage data from the pilot project, the service offered in the new round of applications has been adjusted from ChatGPT Pro to ChatGPT Plus, in order to ensure that the actual needs of the vast majority of participants fall within the quota and thereby extend the benefits of free access to more research teams. Each slot includes the applicant and up to two collaborators, all three of whom can use ChatGPT Plus for free, and this round of funding can cover up to 150,000 researchers.

Since the pilot launched in July this year, the program has attracted 20,000 researchers from 33 countries and regions. Eligible applicants who have already joined the waitlist will receive an email and account activation instructions before the application window opens.

In addition to free access to frontier models, participants will also receive training related to research applications, and the company has promised that by default it will not use data shared through the program to train models. This initiative demonstrates the strategic layout of a leading large-model company in continuing to empower the academic research ecosystem, further accelerating the transformation and innovation of research paradigms by lowering the barrier to using frontier AI tools.
